```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

```

Keeping a local copy of a parquet file is useful when we work with the same file a lot, or run queries that can't be served well by targeted range reads, like scanning whole columns across the file. In those cases the slower initial download is made up for by faster queries afterwards. Another reason for a local copy is that it is available offline.

```{r setup}
library(r2parquet)
Sys.setenv(R2PARQUET_CACHE_PATH = tempfile())
```

The cache lives in the directory named by the `R2PARQUET_CACHE_PATH` environment variable, or in the user cache directory (`tools::R_user_dir("r2parquet", "cache")`) if that is not set. For this vignette we point it at a temporary directory. Cached files mirror their remote location, `r2://bucket/path` as `r2/<account id>/bucket/path` and URLs as `<scheme>/<host>/<path>`, so files from different sources don't collide and one cache directory can serve all projects. Set the environment variable in a project's `.Renviron` for a cache local to that project; `usethis::edit_r_environ("project")` creates and opens that file, and R has to be restarted to pick it up.

To cache a dataset set `cache = TRUE` in `parquet_tbl()`, or cache it explicitly with `cache_parquet()`.

```{r}
census_cma_url <- "https://data.mountainmath.ca/census/2021/lcma000b21f_e.parquet"

geos_cma <- parquet_tbl(census_cma_url, cache = TRUE)
```

This downloads the file if the cache has no current copy and opens the table on the local file. The copy is kept current by its etag: every call with `cache = TRUE` checks the remote file and downloads it again when it changed. We can inspect the cache to see what is available locally.

```{r}
list_parquet_cache()
```

Once a dataset is cached, `parquet_tbl()` reads the copy by default as long as it is current. The `cache` argument chooses how the cache gets used:

* `cache = NULL`, the default, reads the local copy if it is current, and otherwise reads the remote file and warns that the copy is out of date. Paths that have no copy in the cache are read remotely without any check. A copy is checked once per session, the first time its path is read, and later calls reuse the result to cut down on requests and increase performance. Remote data rarely changes, but if it does mid-session, `clear_cache_checks()` makes the next call check again.
* `cache = TRUE` updates the copy if it is out of date, downloading it on first use, and reads it.
* `cache = FALSE` always reads the remote file.
* `cache = "offline"` reads the local copy as it is, without contacting the remote, and fails if there is none. This is for working without a network connection, and for looking at what changed: read the copy with `cache = "offline"` and the current remote file with `cache = FALSE`, compare, then update the copy with `cache = TRUE`.

With the default and with `cache = TRUE`, a copy also gets used, with a warning, when the remote can't be reached.

```{r}
geos_cma <- parquet_tbl(census_cma_url)

geos_cma |>
  dplyr::select(CMAUID, CMANAME, CMATYPE, LANDAREA) |>
  head()
```

Directories of (partitioned) parquet files on R2 get cached the same way, as `r2://bucket/path`. Directories at public URLs can't be listed over https, so they need a `_manifest.json` next to the files, which `upload_parquet()` and `data_to_parquet()` write for directories uploaded to R2 and `write_manifest()` adds to existing ones. It lists the files with their size, etag (the content MD5 for files the package uploaded) and modification time, plus the metadata from the parquet footers, the format is documented in `?write_manifest`.

Listing remote parquet files also states whether the cache holds a current copy.

```{r}
list_parquet(census_cma_url)
```

We can remove the local copy when we don't need the file any more.

```{r}
remove_parquet_from_cache(census_cma_url)
```
